clue.text: Runny glue a shilling? I'm stuck for a name for it!

definitions.text: I'm stuck for a name for it!

parts.note: runny means thin, of a liquid
gum is a glue
a bob is slang for a shilling, the old British coin worth twelve pence

explanation.surface: Someone looking at runny glue wonders what to call the stuff, offering a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, nicknamed a bob. The definition is the exclamation of someone who cannot recall a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingumabob is a placeholder word used when the speaker cannot remember what something is called.

clue.text: Small amount of time used with advantage

parts.note: AD is short for advantage, the tennis score

explanation.surface: A little time put to good use gives you an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A tad is a little bit, a slight quantity of anything.

clue.text: Middle gear learner driver engaged in frightful ride

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so one piece sits inside the other
frightful suggests something in disorder, so the word ride is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner plate on a British car, so a learner driver is L

explanation.surface: A learner driver grinds through the gears on a scary ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' rearranges RIDE as IDER, and 'engaged in' puts L inside it after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is an intermediate gear wheel that sits between two others, transmitting motion without changing the ratio.

clue.text: Sergeant perhaps breaking into song in historic Scots village

indicators.note: breaking into means forcing a way inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a glee is a part-song for unaccompanied voices
a sergeant is an example of an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A sergeant bursts into song in an old Scottish village.
explanation.walkthrough: A glee is an old English part-song for unaccompanied voices. Glencoe in the Highlands is remembered for the massacre of 1692.
explanation.definitionFit: Glencoe is a village in the Scottish Highlands, notorious for the 1692 massacre of the MacDonalds.

clue.text: Mark every killer whale, any number from Balearic area

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, as in the old German currency
every and all are synonyms here
the orca is the killer whale
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A list of tasks: tag every killer whale, however many, around the Balearics.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallorca is the largest Balearic island, so something Mallorcan comes from that part of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Information on jacket smear, black

parts.note: to smear writing is to blur it
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Details about a jacket: a smudge of black on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The jacket is a book's dust jacket, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the promotional text printed on a book's dust jacket.

clue.text: Eastern sweetmeat the French exported from port in Crimea

indicators.note: exported from means sent out of, so these letters leave the port's name

parts.note: Balaklava is a port in Crimea, site of the Charge of the Light Brigade
la is French for the

explanation.surface: A sweet that the French ship out of a Crimean port.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove LA from BALAKLAVA, the first LA, to leave BAKLAVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Baklava is a pastry of filo, nuts and honey syrup from Turkey and the Middle East.

clue.text: Bad actor giving up halfway through major role

indicators.note: giving up halfway through means the second half of the role's name is abandoned

parts.note: Hamlet is one of the great lead roles in theatre

explanation.surface: A poor actor abandons a big part midway.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a performer who overacts, a crude or incompetent player.

clue.text: Try a couple over daughter that's found concealed in trunk

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case
a couple is two
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Attempting a couple of overs for a daughter, about something hidden in a trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Try is in the legal sense: to hear a case in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartwood is the dense inner wood of a tree, hidden inside the outer sapwood of the trunk.

clue.text: Rider of waves swelling a way to south of African country

indicators.note: in a down clue, being to the south of something means coming below it

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
a bubo is an inflamed swelling, as in bubonic plague
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A swelling on the way south from an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malibu board is a long surfboard, the thing a surfer rides on waves.

clue.text: Loud gale circulating round large Welsh town

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece is placed inside the other
circulating suggests moving about, so the words loud gale are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A loud gale swirls around a big Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh place names often end in -AU, a useful pointer when arranging the letters of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolgellau is a market town in Gwynedd, north-west Wales.

clue.text: Bird back around a village in Africa

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is put inside another
back says the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: a lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A bird returns to an African village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LARK into KRAL, and 'around' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kraal is a southern African village of huts, often enclosed by a fence.

clue.text: Backing my company after way of working leather

indicators.note: after says the later pieces follow the first one

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: Supporting my firm's methods for working leather.
explanation.walkthrough: My is an exclamation here, like cor in British speech; reversed it gives ROC.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a fine soft goatskin leather, used for bookbinding.

clue.text: Suspecting obscure fungus almost directly

parts.note: to obscure is to mist, as in misting a window
rust is a fungal disease of plants

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: full can mean directly, as in hit full in the face

explanation.surface: Wary of some strange fungus nearly straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mistrustful means doubting or suspecting others' motives.

clue.text: Source of present British managed boat

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, past tense ran
a tub is a slow clumsy boat

explanation.surface: A British-run boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a British party lucky dip: a tub of bran with small presents buried in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Children pull small gifts out of a bran tub, so it is where a present comes from.

clue.text: Work out volume — something under a foot all round?

indicators.note: all round means surrounding, so the volume letter sits within

parts.note: the sole is the underside of a foot

explanation.surface: Calculating volume, with a teasing question about what lies beneath a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a problem is to work out its answer.

clue.text: Looking well ahead, relative finally settling in without a partner

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: alone or lone means without a partner
gran is a grandmother, a relative

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

parts.note: last letter of settling

explanation.surface: A single relative eventually moving in has an eye on the future.
explanation.walkthrough: Gran is the usual British informal word for a grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range planning or forecasting covers a distant period, so it means thinking far into the future.

clue.text: Be too much to get part of pub mob at soccer turning back?

indicators.note: turning back says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a stretch of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Getting a share of the drunken football crowd turning round costs too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'to get part' into the definition; 'part of' is the hidden-word signal and 'to get' only links, so the definition is 'Be too much'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cost a bomb is British slang for be very expensive, priced far beyond reason.

clue.text: Severe damp I eliminated at the far back of the ship

definitions.text: at the far back of the ship

parts.note: severe and stern are synonyms

indicators.note: eliminated means removed, so the letter I is taken out

parts.note: damp means moist

explanation.surface: Harsh dampness wiped out at the rear of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternmost is the position nearest the stern, the rear end of a ship.

clue.text: Set aside phone receiver

parts.note: to phone someone is to ring them
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: Put the telephone receiver down.
explanation.walkthrough: Receiver looks like part of a phone but is the criminal sense: a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money is to reserve it for one purpose only, guaranteeing it is kept separate.

clue.text: At home getting involved in ordinary diplomacy?

indicators.note: getting involved in means going inside, so these letters sit within the other word

parts.note: in heraldry an ordinary is a simple charge, and the fesse, a horizontal band, is one
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Taking part in everyday tact at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordinary is a heraldic noun here: a basic geometric charge on a shield, like the fesse.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is delicate skill in handling people, the subtle tact of diplomacy.

clue.text: Channels in sea area around island

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the island letter goes inside

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A stretch of sea around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Media are channels of communication such as press, radio and television.

clue.text: Second fall of water? European glacier could end with this

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
rain is water falling

explanation.surface: A second shower of water in Europe, then a note on how glaciers finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal moraine is the ridge of rock debris deposited at a glacier's snout.

clue.text: Melodious South Pacific

parts.note: irenic means pacific, peace-making

explanation.surface: Tuneful sounds of the South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Pacific look like the ocean; it is the adjective meaning peaceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirenic means like a siren's song, sweetly alluring and tuneful.

clue.text: Hero accepting elevation as god

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: El Cid is the Spanish national hero
up means raised, elevated

explanation.surface: A hero taking a promotion to divine status.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid is the Roman deity of love.

clue.text: Knight and men secure ancient upcountry region

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to land something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A knight and his soldiers take an old hill territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Norland is an archaic word for northern land, a region to the north.

clue.text: Note fish out of river to the side of the boat

definitions.text: to the side of the boat

parts.note: A is a musical note

indicators.note: out of means taken away, so the river letter leaves the fish

parts.note: a bream is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Spotting a fish leaving the river beside the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam is a nautical term for a position at right angles to a vessel's length, level with it.

clue.text: Ends financial penalties

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fine is an old word for an end, as in the phrase in fine
second meaning: sums of money paid as punishment

explanation.walkthrough: Fine meaning end survives in phrases like in fine, from Latin finis.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural works both for conclusions in the archaic sense and for monetary punishments.

clue.text: Outstanding concert in marquee, but only one tango

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert

indicators.note: but only one means a single copy of the letter is kept, so one is dropped

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent
T is tango in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An event concert in a big tent, with only one tango dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominent means standing out, conspicuous or eminent.

clue.text: Tiny involuntary convulsion, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so the opening letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: Describing a small spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is a small habitual twitch of the muscles, done without meaning to.

clue.text: What's regularly claimed to be buried in a particular place

definitions.text: be buried in a particular place

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word claimed

explanation.surface: What is said to be buried at some spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth and sixth letters of claimed. A lie is also a false claim, adding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Here lies is the gravestone formula, so to lie is to rest in a grave.

clue.text: Torched mine, excitedly taking in heat

indicators.note: excitedly suggests agitated motion, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mine set on fire in a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: An endothermic reaction absorbs energy from its surroundings, the opposite of exothermic.
